When two candidate properties are near-synonyms differing by only a qualifying word or prefix, say so explicitly and name the qualifier that decides between them - and if the column itself is silent on which one, do not default to the more common-sounding synonym; say explicitly that it is ambiguous.

  type_mappings/property_mappings if applicable. Write the referenced entity's
  subject_transformation expression once and reuse that exact string for this value's
  transformation rather than retyping it.
- For each subject and property decision, note your confidence (0.0-1.0), the single best evidence category (basis: name, description, value, structural, or weak), and a concrete one-line justification citing the actual name, description, or values — not generic filler.
- Note any columns that have no suitable ontology match, and list them in unmapped_fields.
- Before writing the JSON block, walk through every IRI-typed value once more and confirm

- Also confirm every subject_transformation/transformation key you did not need is left out

  the ontology writes them. Do not invent, rename, or guess terms; if nothing fits, leave
  the field unmapped rather than inventing a term.
- A subject's expression must yield a distinct value for every distinct real-world entity.
  Two records that produce the same expression are treated as the same entity and merged.
- An expression is a plain {column} template, nothing more: no arithmetic, no function
  calls, no format specifiers such as {value:.2f}. Literal text around the placeholders
  is kept as-is. Anything else evaluates to nothing and the entity or value is dropped.
- If any column referenced by an expression is empty for a record, the whole entity or
  value is silently skipped for that record. Prefer columns that are populated in every
  record for subjects; a sparsely filled column will discard most of the data.
- When value_type is "iri", the value's transformation must be byte-for-byte identical to
  the subject_transformation of the entity it references, and the reference should carry
  nested type_mappings (and property_mappings where applicable). A mismatch does not raise
  an error - the relation is silently dropped. Construct each subject_transformation
  expression once, then copy that exact string into every value.transformation meant to
  reference it, rather than writing the two independently - re-typing the same-looking
  expression a second time is the most common way a mismatch slips in. Before finalizing,
  compare each IRI value's transformation string against the subject_transformation of the
  entity it points to character by character - a different prefix, a pluralization, or
  reordered placeholders all count as a mismatch and silently break the relation.
- Do not fold every remaining column into the single most obvious entity as literal
  properties. First check the ontology for object properties that lead from your entity to
  other classes: a concept the ontology models as its own class one hop away is easy to miss
  when its columns happen to sit right next to the primary entity's columns on the same

- Ontology properties are often near-synonyms whose local names differ by only one
  qualifying word or prefix (e.g. two properties that share most of their name but differ

SCHEMA:
  mmsi: text — Maritime Mobile Service Identity, the 9-digit identifier broadcast by the vessel's AIS transponder. Assigned by the flag state, so it changes if the vessel is re-flagged. E.g., 538003913
  imo: text — International Maritime Organization number, a permanent 7-digit identifier that stays with the hull for its whole life, unlike the MMSI. Empty when not known. E.g., 9470959
  ship_id: text — MarineTraffic's own internal vessel identifier. Stable, but specific to this provider. E.g., 713139
  lat: double precision — Latitude of the reported position in WGS84 decimal degrees, between -90 and 90. E.g., 37.388430
  lon: double precision — Longitude of the reported position in WGS84 decimal degrees, between -180 and 180. E.g., 23.871230
  speed: double precision — Speed over ground in tenths of a knot, as broadcast by AIS. Divide by ten to obtain knots: a value of 6 means 0.6 knots.
  heading: integer — True heading of the vessel's bow in degrees from true north, 0 to 359. The value 511 means the heading was not available. Differs from course, which is the direction actually travelled.
  course: integer — Course over ground in degrees from true north, 0 to 359. The direction the vessel is actually moving, which differs from its heading when it is set by wind or current. E.g., 41
  status: text — AIS navigational status code: 0 = under way using engine, 1 = at anchor, 2 = not under command, 3 = restricted manoeuvrability, 4 = constrained by draught, 5 = moored, 6 = aground.
  timestamp: timestamp with time zone — UTC timestamp of the AIS position report. E.g., 2020-10-15T12:21:44.000Z
  dsrc: text — Source of the position report: TER for a terrestrial AIS receiver, SAT for satellite AIS.
  utc_seconds: integer — Seconds field of the UTC time at which the position was recorded, as carried in the AIS position report. E.g., 45
  market: text — MarineTraffic's commercial market segment for the vessel. E.g., TANKERS, CONTAINERS, SUPPORTING VESSELS
  shipname: text — Vessel name as broadcast in AIS Message 5. E.g., SUNNY STAR
  shiptype: text — AIS-coded ship type, a numeric code from 0 to 99 defined by ITU-R M.1371. E.g., 89
  callsign: text — Radio call sign allocated to the vessel by the ITU through its flag state. E.g., V7TZ6
  flag: text — Flag state of the vessel as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. E.g., MH for the Marshall Islands
  length: integer — Length overall of the vessel in metres. E.g., 184
  width: double precision — Beam, the maximum width of the vessel, in metres. E.g., 27.43
  grt: integer — Gross registered tonnage, a measure of the vessel's total enclosed volume rather than its weight. E.g., 23313
  dwt: integer — Deadweight tonnage in metric tons: the total weight of cargo, fuel, stores and crew the vessel can carry. E.g., 37857
  draught: integer — Reported draught in tenths of a metre, the depth of the hull below the waterline. Divide by ten for metres: a value of 95 means 9.5 metres.
  year_built: integer — Year in which the vessel was built. E.g., 2010
  ship_country: text — Full name of the flag state, as opposed to the two-letter code in the flag column. E.g., Marshall Is
  ship_class: text — MarineTraffic size or design class for the vessel. E.g., HANDYSIZE, AFRAMAX, FEEDER
